title: World Cup Final Draws 61 Million U.S. Viewers, Smashing All Soccer TV Records
excerpt: Fox's English-language broadcast of Spain's extra-time win over Argentina averaged nearly 39 million viewers, while Telemundo set a Spanish-language record with 23.9 million — triggering a bidding war for future World Cup rights.
body:
More than 61 million Americans tuned in to watch Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in extra time at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, making the 2026 World Cup final the most-watched soccer match in U.S. television history by a massive margin, according to Nielsen Media Research data released by Fox Sports and NBCUniversal on Monday.

Fox's English-language broadcast averaged 38,937,000 viewers, shattering the previous record set just weeks earlier when the United States' round-of-16 loss to Belgium drew a then-unprecedented audience. The final peaked at 51,685,000 viewers between 5:45 and 6:00 PM ET as Spain's Ferran Torres struck in the 103rd minute to seal the trophy for La Roja.

Telemundo's Spanish-language broadcast pulled 23.9 million in Total Audience Delivery, making it the most-watched Spanish-language match in American history. Peacock, NBCUniversal's streaming platform, accounted for 48 percent of Telemundo's total audience delivery across the tournament.

A Tournament That Rewrote the Record Books

The final was merely the culmination of a tournament that demolished every previous benchmark for soccer viewership in the United States. Nine matches during the 2026 World Cup eclipsed the 16.7 million viewers that watched the 2022 final between France and Argentina on Fox — previously the gold standard for U.S. soccer ratings.

Two matches surpassed 30 million viewers, five broke 20 million, and 11 eclipsed 15 million, according to Fox Sports. Across all 104 matches on Fox, FS1 and the free streaming service Tubi, the tournament averaged 7,737,000 viewers — making it the most-watched FIFA World Cup in U.S. history.

Fox's digital coverage generated 17.2 billion content views, the most for any event in network history.

The numbers placed the World Cup final in rarefied territory for American sports broadcasting. Fox's 38.9 million average made it the most-watched English-language telecast of any program outside the NFL since 2016, when 40 million viewers tuned in to Game 7 of the World Series, according to USA Today.

Global Audiences Follow Suit

The viewership surge extended well beyond U.S. borders. In the United Kingdom, the BBC drew a peak audience of 15.8 million for the final, dwarfing ITV's peak of 3.4 million, according to The Sun. The BBC reported 11.1 million streams on iPlayer and reached 42.8 million viewers across the entire tournament.

In Spain, the final averaged 15.4 million viewers with an 86.3 percent audience share across La 1, DAZN and other broadcasters. During extra time, that share climbed to 89.3 percent — making it the second most-watched event in Spanish television history, according to El Periódico Mediterráneo.

Total stadium attendance across the tournament's 104 matches reached 6,810,966, with a 99.7 percent occupancy rate. The final itself drew 80,663 fans to MetLife Stadium.

India Stays Up Past Midnight

The final kicked off at 12:30 AM IST, but Indian cities made special arrangements to accommodate the massive interest. Delhi allowed restaurants and cafés to remain open until 4 AM, while Bengaluru extended operating hours for pubs and bars until 3:30 AM following a request from the National Restaurant Association of India, according to BestMediaInfo.

Zee Entertainment, which holds FIFA broadcast rights for 39 events between 2026 and 2034, carried the tournament on its Unite8 Sports channels and ZEE5 streaming platform. The company claimed its sports portfolio crossed 300 million unique users during the tournament, though these remain company-reported figures.

A Bidding War Is Coming

The staggering U.S. numbers are set to reshape the economics of World Cup broadcasting rights. Telemundo executive Joaquin Duro told Sports Business Journal that the tournament's early success had prompted NBC to consider bidding for both English and Spanish rights for the 2030 and 2034 editions — a departure from the current split between Fox and Telemundo.

"TV viewership records were shattered, both in the host countries and across the globe."

— FIFA statement

ESPN, YouTube, Netflix and Amazon Prime are all reportedly weighing bids, according to USA Today. Netflix has already secured the next two Women's World Cups — in Brazil in 2027 and across the U.S., Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica in 2031 — in both English and Spanish.

Fox and Telemundo acquired their 2026 rights without a competitive bid process back in 2015. The landscape has shifted dramatically since: streaming giants have entered live sports aggressively, and the 2026 numbers have now provided hard evidence that the World Cup can rival traditional American sports franchises in the U.S. market.

What's Next

FIFA has yet to release official global viewership figures for the 2026 tournament, though President Gianni Infantino said at a press conference that TV records were "shattered" worldwide. FIFA projected record revenues exceeding seven billion euros for 2026, a 56 percent increase over the 2022 Qatar World Cup.

The rights negotiations for 2030 (hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay) and 2034 (Saudi Arabia) will be the first true test of whether the 2026 viewership boom translates into a sustained increase in the commercial value of World Cup broadcasting.
